cards.text: Friend, the offerings are in, and the skilled craftsmen get to work on the tabernacle. First up: ten curtains of finely spun linen, with blue, purple and scarlet yarn. Grab your apron, because these folks are about to out-craft every craft fair you've ever walked through.

cards.question: The ten curtains for the tabernacle are linen and colored yarn. What's skillfully worked into them?

cards.text: The ten curtains get joined into two sets of five, with fifty loops of blue material along the edge of each set, lined up across from each other. FIFTY loops lined up perfectly, and I can't line up twelve cookies on a tray without one rolling off to start a new life.

cards.question: Two sets of tabernacle curtains, with fifty loops facing each other. What gets made to join them together?

cards.text: Over the tabernacle goes a tent made of goat hair, eleven curtains of it. Same idea as before: two sets, with fifty loops along the edge of each.

cards.question: The ten inner curtains were joined with gold clasps. The fifty clasps for the goat hair tent are made of something else. What is it?
True or false: the goat hair tent is the very top layer, with nothing else over it.

cards.text: Then come the walls: upright frames of acacia wood, twenty on the south side, twenty on the north and more across the back, each one standing on two silver bases. Crossbars run along the frames, and the frames and crossbars all get overlaid with gold.
Next comes the veil, made of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely spun linen. This crew has gone through more yarn than a craft store on clearance day.

cards.question: True or false: the veil has cherubim skillfully worked into it, just like the ten curtains.

cards.text: The veil hangs on four acacia posts overlaid with gold, with gold hooks. Then comes an embroidered curtain for the entrance to the tent, held up by five posts.

cards.question: The veil's four posts stand on ___ bases, and the five posts at the tent's entrance stand on ___ bases.

cards.text: Now Bezalel, the lead craftsman, builds the ark out of acacia wood. He overlays it with pure gold, inside and out.

cards.question: Bezalel casts four gold rings for the ark's four feet and makes poles overlaid with gold. What are the poles for?

cards.text: Then he makes the mercy seat out of pure gold, with the same length and width as the ark. A gold ark and a solid gold mercy seat, while my fanciest address for years was the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: At each end of the mercy seat, Bezalel hammers something out of gold. What is it?
The two cherubim spread their wings upward, overshadowing the mercy seat. Which way do the cherubim face?

cards.text: Next he makes a table of acacia wood, overlaid with pure gold, with gold rings and gold-covered poles for carrying it. That's two pieces now built with carrying poles, and I RESPECT furniture that's ready to travel, because I sat in one drawer for YEARS.

cards.question: Bezalel makes the utensils for the gold table out of pure gold too. What are they?

cards.text: Then he makes the lampstand out of pure hammered gold. Six branches come out of its sides, three on one side and three on the other.

cards.question: Each branch of the lampstand gets three cups shaped like blossoms. Blossoms from which tree?
True or false: the lampstand's buds and branches are made separately and attached to it afterward.

cards.text: All one piece, every bud and branch, hammered out of pure gold. Friend, I can't even get a cookie off a tray in one piece.

cards.question: The lampstand has six branches, three on each side, plus the lampstand itself. How many lamps does Bezalel make for it?

cards.text: The lampstand and all its utensils come from a talent of pure gold. That is a LOT of shine, friend.
Next comes a small square altar of acacia wood, a cubit long and a cubit wide. He overlays it with pure gold and gives it gold rings and poles for carrying it.

cards.question: What is this small gold altar for?

cards.text: He also makes the sacred anointing oil and the pure, fragrant incense, the work of a perfumer. Build an ark, hammer a lampstand AND mix a fragrance? On my best day, I stamp a cookie.
Bezalel builds the altar of burnt offering from acacia wood, square, five cubits long, five cubits wide and three cubits high. This is not the little incense altar, friend, this one is BIG.

cards.question: At each of the altar's four corners, Bezalel makes a ___.
The ark, the table and the incense altar all got pure gold. What does Bezalel overlay the altar of burnt offering with?

cards.text: All the altar's utensils are bronze too: pots, shovels, sprinkling bowls, meat forks and firepans. Then a bronze mesh grate goes under its ledge, halfway up from the bottom.

cards.question: True or false: like the ark and the table, the altar of burnt offering has rings and poles for carrying it.
True or false: the altar of burnt offering is solid wood all the way through.

cards.text: Next comes the bronze basin and its stand. And the bronze for it comes from somewhere you would NOT expect.

cards.question: Where does the bronze for the basin and its stand come from?

cards.text: Those women served at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, and their MIRRORS became the basin. I've got a mustache this size, friend, so I know exactly what kind of sacrifice that is.

Then he builds the courtyard all around, with curtains of finely spun linen, a hundred cubits on the south and north sides and fifty on the west and east. The posts stand on bronze bases with silver hooks and bands, the entrance gets an embroidered curtain, and every tent peg is bronze.

Then comes the inventory, recorded at Moses' command by the Levites under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest. After all the old receipts I shared that drawer with, these are the first records I've ever been excited about.

cards.question: The inventory names the man who made everything that the LORD had commanded Moses. Who is it?
Working with Bezalel is Oholiab son of Ahisamach, an engraver and designer from the tribe of ___.

cards.text: Then come the totals of gold, silver and bronze, and the silver comes from half a shekel for each of 603,550 men, enough to cast a hundred silver bases. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this build is not done yet.

findings.problem: The card opens with "the offerings are in." That fact comes from Exodus 36:3-7, which is outside this passage, and the card gives it no reference. The card cites only Exodus 36:8.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Fifty bronze pins" is very close to the fifty bronze clasps that join the goat hair tent (Exodus 36:18). A baker could argue that fifty bronze fasteners were made to join curtains. It also hints at the answer to card 6.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The card only asks whether the goat hair tent is the top layer (False). No card ever tells the baker what does go over it: a covering of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather (Exodus 36:19). The baker learns there is another layer but never learns what it is.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Most of Stop 1's choice cards can't be reasoned out from earlier cards. Card 2 (cherubim), card 4 (gold clasps), card 6 (bronze clasps) and card 12 (silver and bronze bases) are pure discovery. Card 7 and card 10 come down to a true-or-false guess. Almost none of the stop's choice cards are informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The card cites Exodus 37:3-5, but the right answer, "Carrying the ark," comes only from Exodus 37:5. Verses 3-4 are setup in the question, not part of the right answer.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: Seven of Stop 2's eight choice cards are multiple choice (cards 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12 and 15). The only other type is one true or false (card 10). There is no fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats the fact the baker just answered on card 10: the buds and branches are all one piece (Exodus 37:22). It adds nothing new and doesn't move the passage forward.

The question "What is this small gold altar for?" uses "this" to point back to card 14, which is no longer on screen. It doesn't say which altar it means, for example that it's the square altar of acacia wood Bezalel makes after the lampstand.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Earlier story cards already give away the answer. Stop 2 card 1 introduces Bezalel as the lead craftsman, and Bezalel is shown building every piece in Stops 2 and 3. That makes "Bezalel" obvious when the question asks who made everything the LORD commanded Moses.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Almost this whole passage (Exodus 36:8-38:31) is building plans for the tabernacle, its furnishings and its courtyard, followed by a material count. The docs list building plans like this as a long stretch. A long stretch gets one summary card, no choice cards and never a stop of its own. The walkthrough uses that treatment for the frames, the courtyard and the totals, but gives the curtains, the ark, the table, the lampstand and the altars many detail choice cards, such as which metal the clasps and bases are made of.
findings.question: When an entire passage is a long stretch, like the building chapters of the tabernacle, how should Prep handle it? Which parts count as moments worth choice cards, and which parts get the one-card summary treatment?
